text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 24 in history.
41 - Gaius Caesar (Caligula), Roman Emperor from 37, was murdered. Caligula, or Little Boots, was a nickname he acquired as a child.

76 - Hadrian, Roman Emperor, born as Publius Aelius Hadrianus. Emperor from 117 to 138, he consolidated Rome's vast empire and strengthened its defences, including the building of a wall between England and Scotland which was named after him.
1076 - The Synod of Worms took place at which German bishops renounced their allegiance to Pope Gregory who in turn excommunicated Henry IV.
1712 - Frederick the Great, King of Prussia from 1740-86, born.
1732 - Pierre-Augustin Caron de Beaumarchais, French playwright and author, born. Best known for "The Marriage of Figaro" and "Barber of Seville", later put to music by Mozart and Rossini.
1746 - Gustav III, King of Sweden from 1771-92, born. During his reign known as the Gustavian Enlightenment, he re-established the monarchy's power over parliament.

1848 - Gold was first discovered in California by James Marshall in Sutters sawmill. Initial press reports were largely ignored. Only when President Polk announced the news in December did the gold rush begin.
1895 - Lord Randolph Churchill, British politician and influential leader of the Conservative Party, died.
1915 - In World War One, the British navy defeated the Germans at the Battle of Dogger Bank.
1920 - Amedeo Modigliani, Italian sculptor and painter, died. In 1918 a Modigliani exhibition which included nudes was closed for indecency.
1935 - Krueger Cream Ale, the first beer to be sold in cans, went on sale in Richmond, Virginia.
1960 - A major insurrection began in Algiers against French policy in the country.
1961 - A U.S. B-52 bomber with two 24-megaton nuclear bombs crashed near Goldsboro, North Carolina.
1965 - Winston Churchill, statesman and wartime British prime minister, died.
1969 - General Franco declared martial law in Spain following disturbances which led to nearly 300 arrests. It lasted until March 25.
1972 - Japanese soldier Shoichi Yokoi was discovered on Guam, having spent 28 years hiding in the jungle thinking the war was still going on.
1978 - Soviet satellite, Cosmos 954, used for ocean surveillance, disintegrated over the remote North-West territories of Canada.
1983 - George Cukor, U.S. film director of "David Copperfield", "Philadelphia Story" and "My Fair Lady", died.
1983 - In Italy, 32 Red Brigade members were jailed for acts of terrorism, including the murder of Aldo Moro.
1987 - U.S. citizen Jesse Turner, computer science professor at Beirut University College, was taken hostage in Lebanon. He was released in October 1991.
1991 - Japan pledged nine billion dollars more to the Gulf War effort which brought angry rejoinders from Iraq.
1995 - A U.S. airman and his 10-year-old son given up for dead in snow-covered mountains in Turkey were found alive after living on snow for nine days.
1996 - Chechen rebels released 42 hostages seized in a raid in southern Russia after a two-week ordeal in which dozens of separatist fighters and many Russian soldiers were killed.
1996 - The Warsaw military prosecutor launched a formal probe into allegations Prime Minister Jozef Oleksy had spied for Moscow.
